extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, federal regulators, electric cooperative leaders, and electric utility stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and stated priorities for public comments and advocacy aimed at preserving electric-grid reliability and affordability, focused on federal and regional policy, regulation, and investment decisions affecting electric cooperatives and rural communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize reliability and affordability
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy agenda should prioritize reliability and affordability for American families and businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly urges leaders to 'prioritize reliability right out of the gate' and adopt 'smart energy policies that keep the lights on.' Comments should stress that policy choices must center on maintaining reliable, reasonably priced power for consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in American energy production, manufacturing, and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies should prioritize investment in American energy production, manufacturing and infrastructure as crucial to rural community wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for coordinated approaches that ensure energy projects can be built efficiently, effectively, and at reasonable cost; emphasize economic and community benefits of domestic energy investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate policymakers and regulators on reliability implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers need awareness of the reliability implications of policy-driven energy transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite NERC: 'Ensuring reliability during and after policy driven transitions should be a key consideration' and recommend outreach/education to regulators so policy choices account for reliability tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard electric reliability against regulatory threats
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the electric grid from regulatory actions (e.g., EPA rules) that could force premature retirements of always-available generation and jeopardize reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to NERC assessments showing elevated shortfall risks; argue that rules relying on unproven technology or unrealistic timelines can undermine reliability and should be reconsidered or delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform and streamline federal permitting and siting
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernize and streamline federal permitting and siting processes to eliminate excessive regulatory burdens and produce predictable, timely decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for procedural reforms that accelerate construction of energy projects while preserving necessary environmental and safety reviews; emphasize permitting as a barrier to deploying reliability-improving infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance wildfire protection and grid hardening
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass legislation and take actions to improve grid hardening and wildfire mitigation procedures on utility rights-of-way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite proposals like the Fix Our Forests Act (H.R. 8790) as examples; recommend funding and regulatory changes to reduce wildfire risk to transmission and distribution assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect Lower Snake River dams and similar hydropower resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve hydropower assets like the Lower Snake River dams as sources of reliable, affordable, carbon-free electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that breaching dams would remove dependable generation and harm regional reliability and affordability—advocate legal and policy measures to protect such assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend and preserve direct-pay tax credits for co-ops
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain direct-pay tax credits that provide direct federal payments to electric co-ops deploying new energy technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stress the importance of direct-pay for co-ops' ability to invest in carbon capture, nuclear, storage, renewables and other technologies without traditional tax-equity structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain USDA 'New ERA' and similar funding for innovative projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect funding for innovative energy projects under programs like the Department of Agriculture’s Empowering Rural America (New ERA) Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate continued federal support for rural innovation projects that enhance reliability, resilience, and economic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectively use Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use remaining IIJA funds to improve electric infrastructure, enhance grid resilience and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend targeted IIJA deployment to transmission, hardening, and resilience projects that provide measurable reliability benefits to rural customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote transmission planning and expansion focused on load-serving needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission planning and expansion should meet the needs of load-serving entities (LSEs) and the consumers they serve, with fair cost-allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urge FERC and states to prioritize projects that address transmission constraints affecting co-ops and to adopt transparent, equitable cost-allocation and regional flexibility in planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize interconnection for load-serving entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Give priority to LSEs seeking to interconnect new generation to the grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend procedural or policy changes so LSEs (including co-ops) face fewer barriers and delays when interconnecting resources needed for reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revamp resource adequacy measurement and forecasting
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC should update how it measures and forecasts resource adequacy to reflect current dynamics (load growth, retirements, variable resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should press for adequacy metrics that account for variable and energy-limited resources, large new commercial loads, and regional specifics rather than outdated assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a diverse resource portfolio ('all of the above')
rubrics_metrics.description: A diverse mix of resources—including dispatchable, baseload, and variable resources—is critical to reliability and affordability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for policies that do not prematurely remove dispatchable resources and that support balanced portfolios (gas, coal where appropriate, nuclear, hydro, storage, renewables) to meet peak and extreme conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance cost and reliability for consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and planning decisions must consider consumer costs — the objective is to strike a balance between affordability and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight that many co-op members are in persistent-poverty counties; request cost-impact analyses of major regulatory changes and support options that preserve affordable service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare operations for high demand and low-resource conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grid operators, generation owners, and authorities should prepare for high electricity demand and low wind conditions, winterize units, and increase coordination around generation fuels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Echo NERC recommendations: winter readiness, fuel assurance, operational coordination, and demand-preparation measures to avoid emergency conditions and minimize outages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in demand-side management and energy efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase investment in demand-side programs and energy-efficiency initiatives to reduce peak load and improve system reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite EKPC’s plans to double such investments and programs that cut MWh and reduce winter peak as examples of actions that reduce system stress and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use federal resilience grants (e.g., DOE GRIP/START) to strengthen transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage DOE Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships and similar grants to build/rebuild/reconductor transmission, increase transfer capacity and deploy advanced conductors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend applying for and directing GRIP/START funds to projects that demonstrably increase transfer capacity, harden lines, and support regional reliability for rural utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose regulations relying on inadequately demonstrated technologies or unrealistic timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory requirements that hinge on unproven technologies (e.g., large-scale carbon capture) or infeasible compliance timelines risk reliability and economic harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the EPA Power Plant Rule example: capture 90% by 2032 for some units and co-firing requirements that may be unachievable; urge courts/regulators to reassess or slow implementation to avoid grid harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider cumulative and regional impacts when evaluating reliability risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers and regulators should consider the cumulative impact of load growth, plant retirements, and the proliferation of variable resources when assessing reliability risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask regulators to account for the interaction of multiple trends (data centers, electrification, retirements) and to permit regional flexibility and local prioritization of solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize projects and policies that deliver long-term member equity and cost stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Investments should aim to deliver long-term reliability, cost-competitive electricity, and 'equity' returns for cooperative members over decades, not just short-term gains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples like AECC’s investments in gas and solar to argue for planning horizons and investment strategies that protect members from volatile costs and capacity shortfalls.
